newsitem.title: COSTA RICA: Costa Rica fears more coffee losses after Lili.
newsitem.headline: Costa Rica fears more coffee losses after Lili.

text.p: Costa Rica's 1996-1997 coffee crop could suffer further losses after torrential rains flooded one coffee zone this week, the executive director of Costa Rica's Coffee Institute (ICAFE) said Thursday.
"One of the most flood-hit zones from the rains this week was Perez Zeledon, where 16 percent of the national coffee crop is produced," Guillmero Canet told Reuters.
Canet said German Urea, the growers' representative from the zone, told ICAFE Wednesday said some mature beans in the area did not hold up in the strong rains and fell from trees.
"Urea is a grower from Perez Zeledon and he told us that they are only just starting to evaluate the scale of damage which still has not been quantified," Canet said.
Hurricane Lili lurked off Costa Rica's Caribbean coast October 12-16 as a tropical storm before edging northwards and gaining strength, although moving away from Central America.
The unquantified damages from Lili come on top of the losses registered after the passage of Hurricane Cesar in mid-August.

ICAFE reported losses from Cesar totaled around five percent of the national crop, or 145,000 46-kg bags, from an original estimate for this cycle of a harvest totaling 3.1 million bags, or quintals, as they are known in the region.
Canet said the Lili damage adds to the problems the country faces because of damaged infrastructure, principally, access roads to plantations.
"What is worse is that we were scarcely recovering from that emergency. Roads have not been completely repaired, and repairs, in some cases, have been damaged again," Canet said.
